facts.text: Yaddo, a 400‑acre artists’ community founded by financier Spencer Trask and author Katrina Trask, sits in Springs.
The Pollock‑Krasner House, where Jackson Pollock and Lee Krasner worked, became a National Historic Landmark in 1999 and now serves as a study center.
Before Europeans arrived, the Montaukett people used Springs’ freshwater springs, ponds, and coastal resources for fishing and seasonal agriculture.
The original Saratoga Race Course track opened in 1833 on East Avenue, perpendicular to today’s course, founded by John Hunter and William R.
The 1832 arrival of the Saratoga and Schenectady Railroad brought thousands of travelers to Springs’ mineral springs and resort hotels.
Springs’ official slogan, “Health, History, and Horses,” reflects its legacy as a spa town, racing hub, and cultural center.
